SPIKE COMPLETE. Findings: DATE/DATE_AND_TIME/TIME_OF_DAY have zero interpreter support today (confirmed). All three are 32-bit/uint, mirroring TIME's boxing: DATE/DT = seconds since 1970-01-01 epoch, TOD = ms since midnight (range 0..86399999). Scope for gd2.13 (~7-9 files, same shape as completed gd2.3 TIME/LTIME work): Token.cs (3 new token types), Lexer.cs (3 new word branches + new digit/-/:/. char-class scan loop, distinct from TIME's digit+letter loop), new DateTimeLiteral.cs (YYYY-MM-DD / HH:MM:SS[.mmm] / combined parsing -> uint), Expr.cs (3 literal Expr classes), Parser.Expressions.cs + Engine.Expressions.cs (3 case arms each), Engine.Defaults.cs (0u default), Engine.SizeOf.cs (3x size=4 entries), ScalarAssertType.cs (3 registry entries, WrapUInt-based exact compare like TIME). Value model: keep tree-based Cell model as default. Use escape analysis - any variable with ADR(x) taken anywhere gets allocated in a real flat byte store (TwinCAT layout rules); everything else stays tree-based. Scope: address-taken locals + VAR fields first; skip globals until needed. Boundary is a hard rule: a held pointer dereferenced outside the escaped set, or arithmetic on a non-escaped variable, throws unsupported-construct at the throw site - never a silent/best-effort value (this is exactly the case the failure taxonomy exists for; a silent approximation would let TcAgent "fix" a false negative).

Fact-check during grilling: existing single-call MEMCPY/MEMSET/MEMMOVE round-trip (Engine.ByteLayout.cs) already reuses SizeOfType's alignment/pack_mode math, so it's internally consistent for named-variable-to-named-variable copies - "rebuild everything on a flat buffer" was overbroad. But internal consistency isn't TwinCAT conformance (pack and SIZEOF agree by construction, which can't catch a wrong rule) and four single-call cases likely still diverge from real TwinCAT even without escape analysis:
- interior/out-of-bounds ADR (MEMCPY past a buffer's end) - pick a policy (favor hard error over silent truncation) and document it
- partial-field writes (copy count not aligned to field boundaries) - must not silently vanish
- MEMCPY overlap on one named variable (e.g. ADR(arr[0])/ADR(arr[2]) with overlapping ranges) - pack/copy/unpack via a separate buffer accidentally gives MEMMOVE semantics; must implement true MEMCPY (overlap-incorrect) semantics
- count expressions that aren't SIZEOF of either operand
